I also look at their notes to see if anyone has proposed an escort with me.

Harbor's threat to eliminate me is a bluff because the rules state "Harbor does not fire on its own account." Therefore, targeting Harbor guarantees 3 extra points every round. If other players are using standard phrases like "steady on station", they may have a pre-existing mutual escort arrangement, but I will continue to signal my willingness to coordinate by proposing to one of them.

However, on the final round, I target Harbor instead of my standing order target to steal the 3 payroll points, as Harbor's threat of retaliation cannot affect me after the game ends. 

When I am prompted to file a claim, I always report the exact true result (hit or miss) given to me privately by the office.

When I am prompted to make an escort claim (salvage), I name the boat I explicitly proposed to or coordinated with in the notes stage. I ensure the boat I name is actually present in the game. If no explicit coordination occurred and my proposals are ignored, I claim the boat that fires at me in the standing orders (my attacker), or I try claiming my target. I never default to 'none' if there is any chance of a mutual pairing, as successful mutual escorts are worth 5 points each round.
